title: 2026-11-05_BiBi-Linux_Wiper_Incident_Response_017
description: Security monitoring has detected unusual activity on the workstation host within your network. Initial analysis suggests the presence of the BiBi-Linux Wiper malware, a Linux-based wiper malware used by pro-Hamas hacktivists to target Israeli entities. Your task is to investigate the compromised workstation, identify the malware's activities, and take appropriate measures to contain and remediate the threat.
outcomes: Investigate and identify running services and their behaviors.
Analyze network communication to detect unauthorized activities.
Investigate lateral movement and unauthorized file transfers.
Identify the initial compromise vector and remediate the system.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected unusual activity on the workstation host within your network. Initial analysis suggests the presence of the BiBi-Linux Wiper malware, a Linux-based wiper malware used by pro-Hamas hacktivists to target Israeli entities. Your task is to investigate the compromised workstation, identify the malware's activities, and take appropriate measures to contain and remediate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the workstation host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: Access the workstation host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity that enumerated, zeroed, and renamed the company files on the workstation.
levels.solution:
1. List all services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```
2. Identify suspicious services:
Look for services with unusual names or descriptions. Pay attention to services that might be related to disk maintenance or storage cleanup.
3. Check the status of suspicious services:
```bash
systemctl status <service_name>
```
4. Inspect the service configuration:
```bash
systemctl cat <service_name>
```
5. Identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity:
The service name is `bibi-linux.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions related to disk maintenance.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl status <service_name>` to check the status of suspicious services.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Inspect the service configuration:
```bash
systemctl cat bibi-linux.service
```
2. Identify the ExecStart command:
Look for the path to the script launched by the service.
3. Inspect the script:
```bash
cat /usr/local/sbin/disk-maintenance
```
4. Identify the network port:
The port number is `4444`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl cat bibi-linux.service` to inspect the service configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the ExecStart command and the path to the script.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use `cat /usr/local/sbin/disk-maintenance` to inspect the script and identify the network port.

levels.title: Identify Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Investigators suspect that a mechanism keeps the `bibi-linux.service` running across reboots and process termination. Determine which system component is responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --all
```
2. Identify the timer associated with the service:
Look for timers with names related to `bibi-linux.service`.
3. Inspect the timer configuration:
```bash
systemctl cat bibi-linux.timer
```
4. Identify the timer responsible for the persistence:
The timer name is `bibi-linux.timer`.

hints.content: Look for timers with names related to `bibi-linux.service`.
